newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peronists feel pressure from mafia "witch-hunt".
newsitem.headline: Peronists feel pressure from mafia "witch-hunt".

text.p: Two top government ministers said on Wednesday they were targets of a "witch-hunt" after calls for congressional hearings to explain their contacts with a tycoon with alleged mobster connections who is linked to a sensational murder case.

Justice Minister Elias Jassan and Interior Minister Carlos Corach complained of a "McCarthyist witch-hunt" after it was shown that both had received phone calls from businessman Alfredo Yabran, whom police are investigating in connection with the murder of a news photographer.
"The Argentine people feel indignant," Frepaso opposition leader Carlos Alvarez said, pointing out that Jassan had denied even knowing Yabran, a private postal business mogul.

Both members of President Carlos Menem's government stand accused by ex-Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo of manipulating the courts to protect Yabran, whom Cavallo and the opposition accuse of being "the head of the mafia" in Argentina.

Police have named Yabran as the main object of investigations into who ordered the killing of Noticias magazine photographer Jose Luis Cabezas in January, for which a former policeman has been charged.

Yabran has not been charged with any crime and has taken out advertisements pleading that he is no "Al Capone," just a "simple postman." He is suing Cavallo and three witnesses in the Cabezas case for slander and allegedly faking evidence.
Jassan publicly denied knowing Yabran but changed his tune this weekend after newspapers published details of 100 calls made to his mobile phone from Yabran's offices.
With La Nacion newspaper demanding he resign, he said he "didn't lie" when he said he did not know Yabran: "What I was saying was that I was not his friend."
Menem, facing key elections in Congress in October, backed his ministers and appeared in photos laughing with Jassan.

Opposition Radical Party leader Rodolfo Terragno said such behaviour "shows a dramatic difference between what society thinks and the government's attitude." His party tabled an urgent motion have Corach and Jassan questioned in Congress.

Cavallo, the target of a Peronist Party press and poster campaign accusing him of "Nazi tactics" and "disloyalty" for accusing former cabinet colleagues, said: "This strategy of attacking me ... was first decided by Yabran and now President Menem and some of his ministers are following it, as if they had signed a contract."
